payload.previous_proof_nl: Let x be any real number, and set m = floor(x). By the definition of the floor function, m is an integer, m ≤ x, and m is the greatest integer with this property. We claim that x < m + 1. If not, then x ≥ m + 1. Since m + 1 is also an integer and m + 1 ≤ x, this would contradict the maximality of m as the greatest integer less than or equal to x. Therefore x < m + 1 = floor(x) + 1. Since x was arbitrary, the statement holds for all real x.

result_payload.proof_nl: Let x be any real number and set m = floor(x). By the definition of the floor function, m is an integer, m <= x, and m is the greatest integer with this property. Suppose, for contradiction, that x >= m + 1. Then m + 1 is also an integer, and m + 1 <= x. This contradicts the maximality of m as the greatest integer less than or equal to x. Hence x < m + 1 = floor(x) + 1. Since x was arbitrary, the statement holds for every real number x.
result_payload.proof_summary: Using the defining maximality property of the floor function, any assumption that x is at least floor(x)+1 contradicts that floor(x) is the greatest integer <= x.
